options: A virtual table that fetches data on every query
A database object that physically stores the output of a query
A temporary table dropped at the end of a session
An index built on a regular view
A file exported from a table
questions.explanation: A materialised view is a database object that stores the output of a query physically, unlike a regular view which is virtual.

questions.stem: How does a materialised view differ from a regular view?
options: A materialised view cannot be queried with SELECT
A materialised view is always smaller
A materialised view physically stores the data, whereas a regular view is a virtual table derived from a SELECT query
A regular view stores data but a materialised view does not
A materialised view cannot join multiple tables
questions.explanation: Unlike a regular view, which is virtual, a materialised view stores the result set in a table-like structure within the database.

questions.stem: What does a materialised view represent in terms of timing?
options: Live data reflecting every change instantly
Data as it will be after the next scheduled load
A random sample of the underlying tables
A snapshot of the data at the time it was last refreshed
Only the rows inserted since creation
questions.explanation: A materialised view is a snapshot of the data at the time the materialised view was last refreshed.

questions.stem: Are materialised views automatically updated when the underlying data changes?
options: Yes, always in real time
Yes, but only for inserts
Only if they contain an aggregate
Yes, whenever a SELECT is run against them
No, they typically need to be refreshed periodically
questions.explanation: Materialised views are not automatically updated; you typically refresh them periodically to synchronise with the base tables.

questions.stem: Which command updates a materialised view with the latest data from the underlying tables?
options: REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW EmployeeProfile;
UPDATE MATERIALIZED VIEW EmployeeProfile;
RELOAD VIEW EmployeeProfile;
SYNC VIEW EmployeeProfile;
REBUILD VIEW EmployeeProfile;
questions.explanation: REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW EmployeeProfile; updates the materialised view with the latest data from the underlying tables.

questions.stem: Why can materialised views significantly improve query performance?
options: They compress the underlying tables
They store precomputed results, reducing the need to perform complex calculations on the fly
They lock the base tables during queries
They run queries on a separate server
They remove the need for indexes
questions.explanation: Performance optimisation comes from storing precomputed results so complex calculations need not be performed on the fly.

questions.stem: For which scenario are materialised views described as particularly useful?
options: Real-time transaction processing
Enforcing referential integrity
Offline analysis on a specific snapshot of the data without querying the live database
Storing unstructured documents
Managing user permissions
questions.explanation: Materialised views are particularly useful for offline analysis on a specific snapshot without querying the live database.

questions.stem: When are materialised views especially effective for aggregation and summary?
options: When the underlying data changes every second
When the tables have no primary keys
When queries are run very rarely
When the underlying data changes infrequently compared to the frequency of querying
When the data is stored in external files
questions.explanation: They are effective for aggregating and summarising data where the underlying data changes infrequently compared with how often it is queried.

questions.stem: How might a regular view and a materialised view be used together in one application?
options: The materialised view enforces security while the regular view stores data
Both must always be refreshed at the same time
The regular view is used only for inserts and the materialised view for deletes
The materialised view replaces the regular view entirely
A regular view for real-time querying and a materialised view for periodic reporting or analytical purposes
questions.explanation: You might use a regular view for real-time querying and a materialised view for periodic reporting or analytics, depending on requirements.

questions.stem: How is a materialised view queried once it has been created?
options: Just like any other table or view, for example SELECT * FROM EmployeeProfile WHERE Age > 25;
Only through a stored procedure
Only after it has been converted to a regular table
Through a special MATERIALIZED SELECT statement
By reading its underlying data file directly
questions.explanation: Once created, a materialised view can be queried just like any other table or view, leveraging the precomputed results.
